messages:
lee: FYI: we just saw a failing rollout for the "minimal-runtime" base image on staging nodes. Containers crash on startup and the audit entries show the image signer metadata never got attached. Error snippet from pod: 
```
Mar 14 09:02:11 dockerd[123]: error setting cgroups: permission denied
Mar 14 09:02:12 kms-client: UnwrapKey failed: PERMISSION_DENIED (projects/company/keys/image-signer)
Mar 14 09:02:12 audit: signer_identity: ""
```
anika: h/t, this smells like two correlated regressions: 1) systemd/cgroup v2 changes in the new image that break rootless container startup, 2) the builder's ephemeral SA lost KeyDecrypt perms after the last keystore policy cleanup.
sam: I pulled node journal. The stack fails at pivot_root/cgroup mount, then container runtime exits. The KMS call happens during layer verification which runs as part of the init hook; if the init hook can't run in the exited process, signer info won't be posted.
lee: runbook decision options? rollback image or adjust node flags?
anika: short-term mitigation: restart canary with CONTAINER_ROOTLESS=0 and NODE_CGROUP_MODE=hybrid to emulate old behaviour. Also schedule an IAM audit: check the binding for serviceAccount:ci-builder@infra.svc to roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter on the keystore project.
sam: here's a quick IAM check we ran: 
```
# gcloud projects get-iam-policy keystore-prod --flatten="bindings[].members" \
  --filter="bindings.role:roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter" \
  --format="value(bindings.members)" | grep ci-builder@infra.svc || echo "missing"
"
ops-bot: rollout-monitor: canary-9002 -> FAILED (exit 1). See logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/rollouts/9002 :warning:

anika: if IAM binding is missing we can temporarily add a narrow binding scoped to the single key: 
```
gcloud kms keys add-iam-policy-binding image-signer \
  --project=keystore-prod --location=global --keyring=signers \
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-builder@infra.svc \
  --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyDecrypter
```
Note: prefer granting at key-level rather than whole project. We'll follow up with least-privilege review.
lee: good. also we should add an admission check in CI that fails a new base image if it moves cgroup default from v1->v2 without a compatibility flag. Small preflight: run a tiny container that prints /proc/self/cgroup and try a simple unprivileged mount.
sam: adding to that, propose a quick telemetry change: when the signer attach step runs, emit an explicit audit event success/failure that is shipped to the central audit pipeline. Right now silence looks identical to "didn't run".
anika: agreed. I'll open a short RFC for audit event telemetry and a follow-up for IAM guardrails.
oncall: INC-2389 opened to track: https://tickets.internal/INC-2389  oncall will coordinate rollback if needed.
lee: redeploying canary with NODE_CGROUP_MODE=hybrid now. will post results. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
